— John Kicklighter (@JohnKicklighter) February 4, 2019 Enjoy those tailwinds while they last says our call of the day , from chilly Montreal, where Yves Lamoureux, president of macroeconomic research firm Lamoureux & Co. , has an update on a prescient call he made last autumn .
First, some background. In January 2016, Lamoureux predicted the Dow would top 25,000 within three or four years, which it did at the start of last year. The rest of 2018 saw the index moving back and forth across that big level. In October, he predicted the Dow would eventually hit 40,000, but forecast a big “panic event” would occur first, as he warned investors to stay out of stocks in 2019.
His new call has to do with that “big panic event,” round 2: “The shock we had in November, December was the first shock and the market realizing that we’re floating too high and [markets] have gotta come back down. There’s another drop to come, which will create tremendous opportunity,” he said in a Monday interview with MarketWatch.
Lamoureux thinks that second shakeout will happen in the next six months, with China slowdown signs and/or a yuan devaluation a couple of things he thinks might trigger a pullback. He says 21,000 for the Dow would sent him on a stock-shopping spree.
Read: U.S. investors eye China stimulus as a key to bull-market longevity
In his opinion, some stocks should be a lot lower than they are, and indexes aren’t quite telling the truth that can be found by taking a closer look at the charts, such as the one below showing the billions lost in market cap for Apple AAPL, +1.20% and Nvidia NVDA, -0.38% :
FactSet He says the first big drop, such as the one seen late last year, tends to make investors question the market, but not panic, finding some reassurance as stocks bounce.
“If we ever get one more drop then you get ridiculous prices…reductions from the top. That’s what creates the next buying opportunity,” says Lamoureux, who’s is ready as he got out of stocks 100% in January.
He suggests portfolios should reduce exposure to stocks, and says investors should have some cash at the ready, and not tied up elsewhere, such as bonds, because when the big drop happens again, everything will go down.
Last word goes to Joel Kruger, currency strategist at LMAX Exchange, who has some here-and-now perspective on the market: “We believe the paradigm has shifted into 2019 and a stock market that had once been a buy on dips for higher lows and higher highs, is now a sell into rallies for lower highs and lower lows.
“While it’s true investors have found comfort in the Fed’s more cautious outlook, we don’t believe this will be enough to offset the fact that monetary policy accommodation tools have been exhausted post-2008 crisis and investor immunity to downside risk is no longer what it once was,” he said.

Europe stocks SXXP, +1.41% are higher. Much of Asia is on holiday, but Aussie stocks XJO, +1.95% took off after the central bank left rates unchanged.
The chart Tailwinds for this stock market? We got ‘em. Our chart(s) of the day come compliments of The Daily Shot , which offers up this pair that show how lots of investors are anywhere but equities right now:
First up, TD Ameritrade’s Investor Movement Index, which shows the levels of enthusiasm for stocks by individual investors is looking pretty depressed lately:
Next is a Bank of America Merrill Lynch chart, which shows a fairly high level of money sitting in Treasury bills, which tend to be considered a haven in times of economic uncertainty, of which there isn’t a shortage right now:
The buzz Fed Chairman Jerome Powell and a couple of other Fed officials, dined with POTUS and Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin at the White House. But don’t get your hopes up, because the only thing juicy about it was the steaks.
Alphabet GOOGL, -0.89% is getting dinged after results showed an earnings beat — driven by a mysterious investment gain — but also a big jump in spending by Google .
Elsewhere, Archer Daniels ADM, -6.14% results have disappointed , while BP BP, +3.33% BP., +5.17% swung to a forecast and investors are liking that .
After Tuesday’s close, we’ll get results from Snapshot parent Snap SNAP, -0.51% which has had some trouble at the helm in early 2019, which could make for an interesting conference call. Disney DIS, -0.04% will also report late.
GlaxoSmithKline GSK, +1.20% and Merck KGaA MRK, +0.39% have announced a $4.23 billion immunotherapy deal.
POTUS is getting ready to nominate one of World Bank’s biggest critics to lead it . Meanwhile, Federal prosecutors have ordered the Trump inaugural committee to hand over documents, in a probe over donors and spending .
The economy Catch-up data coming with the December trade balance, followed by PMI Markit services and the ISM nonmanufacturing index.
Then at 9 p.m. we’ll get POTUS’s State of the Union address, where we could get a decision on a wall emergency and North Korea summit details. Some say look out for the speech to drive a wedge between Republicans.
